gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 13?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 13 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest DWD and ECMWF model runs converge on a Munich daytime maximum near 31°C today, driven by a stable high-pressure ridge and southwesterly warm advection under mostly clear skies and light winds. This setup produces strong surface heating that exceeds the city’s late-August climatological mean of 24–26°C, with ensemble guidance showing only modest spread around 30–32°C tied to minor boundary-layer moisture differences. Traders weight the narrow 30–31°C window most heavily given the model consensus and current observational trends. Resolution could shift only if an unforecasted increase in cloud cover or a sudden wind shift reduces peak insolation before official measurements finalize the daily high.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and AccuWeather point to a maximum temperature of 29–30°C in Tokyo on August 15, driven by the strengthening Pacific High that has produced above-normal summer temperatures across Honshu. This subtropical ridge promotes subsidence and clear to partly cloudy skies, yet scattered showers expected midday could limit peak heating by increasing cloud cover and evaporative cooling. Urban heat island effects from Tokyo's dense infrastructure add 1–2°C locally compared to rural baselines, while high humidity near 80% sustains warmth without altering the dry-bulb reading used for market resolution. Model consensus shows limited day-to-day variability at this lead time, with any shift in steering flow or precipitation timing the main variables that could favor 28°C or 31°C instead.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from the Met Office and ECMWF place London's August 15 maximum near 26–28°C under a mix of sunny intervals and scattered showers, with limited diurnal heating from modest Atlantic airflow and variable cloud. This tight clustering around 26–27°C reflects genuine uncertainty in afternoon convective development and exact frontal timing rather than strong divergence among models. After an intense early-August heatwave that pushed readings above 35°C, cooler maritime air has moderated conditions while still leaving the day slightly above the long-term August average. Traders weigh these factors against historical late-summer variability, where small shifts in boundary-layer moisture or insolation can swing the peak by 1–2°C. Official Met Office observations at 18:00 BST will resolve the market.

Historical analogs for similar synoptic patterns in Tokyo during peak summer show maxima clustering in the upper 20s when instability and moisture are present.

Recent model runs have remained consistent, with no signals of clearing skies or stronger subsidence that could push readings to 30°C or above (combined probability ~9%). Lower outcomes remain negligible given the established warm airmass. The market-implied odds therefore embed the latest observational trends and short-range forecast consensus, with resolution hinging on the official 24-hour maximum recorded by JMA stations.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 14 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Updated model runs over the next 24 hours ahead of market resolution will determine whether the peak registers at the upper or lower end of the favored range.

Historical August climatology for the region shows mean daily maxima of 23–25°C, underscoring the current anomalously warm setup. Model spread remains modest but sensitive to exact cloud timing and wind shifts, with updated runs from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts expected before resolution to refine the 30–33°C range.

gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in London on August 14?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 14 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the London City Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/gb/london/EGLC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This aligns with the market’s tight clustering around 33–34°C, reflecting both the forecast consensus and the urban heat-island amplification typical of central London stations. Broader summer 2026 warmth—already producing multiple days above 30°C—provides supporting context, yet model spread on shower timing and exact wind shifts keeps a modest probability attached to 32°C or 35°C. Updated observational data through midday today will further narrow resolution criteria for the daily maximum.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent model consensus and official agency guidance point to a post-heatwave cooldown setting up a maximum around 26–27 °C in London on 15 August 2026.** After an intense spell that produced a provisional 38.1 °C at Kew Gardens earlier in the week, a thundery breakdown and northerly flow are bringing fresher maritime air across southern England. The Met Office explicitly forecasts a 27 °C daytime maximum for Saturday, while BBC Weather guidance centers on 26 °C; these small differences arise mainly from the precise timing of any residual cloud or light showers and the strength of the north-westerly breeze, which can suppress the peak by 1 °C.

Ensemble output from both ECMWF and GFS shows tight clustering in the mid- to upper-20s, with limited spread reflecting modest uncertainty in boundary-layer mixing and any late-day convective development. Historical climatology for mid-August places the long-term average maximum near 22–23 °C, so the current setup remains above normal but far below the preceding heatwave values. With resolution hinging on the official recorded high (typically the highest hourly or synoptic observation at a designated London station), traders are weighting the two leading bins almost equally because forecast error margins of ±1 °C are common at this range and the latest runs continue to straddle the 26–27 °C threshold.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus centers on 26–27°C as London’s highest temperature on August 15, with market-implied probabilities reflecting tight ensemble spreads from Met Office and ECMWF models. Primary drivers include a weak ridge of high pressure promoting light winds and partial cloud cover, limiting strong daytime heating while allowing urban heat-island effects to add 1–2°C locally. Recent model runs show modest upward adjustments from drier boundary-layer conditions, yet forecast uncertainty remains elevated due to potential overnight cloud or Atlantic moisture intrusions that could cap maxima near 26°C or permit brief clearing to reach 28°C. Historical August averages of 22–23°C provide context, but current steering patterns and soil-moisture anomalies favor the narrow range now priced by traders. Updated model guidance and Met Office briefings expected later today will likely refine these probabilities.

Historical August averages of 22–23°C provide context, but current steering patterns and soil-moisture anomalies favor the narrow range now priced by traders. Updated model guidance and Met Office briefings expected later today will likely refine these probabilities.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 15 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for Tokyo's highest temperature on August 15, 2026, centers on 29–31°C, reflecting JMA and international model consensus for a typical midsummer day with highs near the long-term average of ~31°C.** 

Current forecasts indicate a maximum around 29–30°C (roughly 84–86°F), consistent with seasonal patterns of subtropical high pressure, urban heat island effects, and moderate humidity levels that often cap afternoon peaks unless strong insolation or clear skies develop. Recent JMA guidance and extended outlooks show stable conditions without an intense heat dome or typhoon influence, keeping the distribution tightly clustered. 

Slight upward bias toward 30–31°C arises from potential localized warming in central Tokyo districts, while lower probabilities for 32°C+ or below 28°C align with historical rarity of extremes on single August days absent major synoptic shifts. Updated model runs closer to the event will likely refine these implied probabilities as diurnal heating and any cloud cover become clearer.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 16 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Lower odds on 84-85°F reflect uncertainty in exact peak timing and station-specific readings, while probabilities above 88°F remain minimal absent stronger high-pressure ridging or urban heat-island amplification. Official resolution will use verified observations from primary reporting stations, with final data releases expected shortly after sunset.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for Tokyo's highest temperature on August 16 centers on the 29–30°C range, reflecting a tight balance between seasonal heat and moderating factors like cloud cover and showers.** 

Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts for that Sunday show a maximum near 31°C under cloudy skies with occasional scattered showers, yet model variability in timing and extent of cloudiness keeps probabilities split between 29°C and 30°C. A strengthened Pacific High is sustaining above-normal summer temperatures across Honshu, but localized reductions in solar insolation from increased moisture and potential convective activity can trim peak readings by 1–2°C. Tokyo’s urban heat island effect amplifies baseline warmth, while high humidity (often exceeding 75%) influences perceived conditions without altering the official dry-bulb maximum. With resolution hinging on precise observational data from the Japan Meteorological Agency, the narrow spread between leading outcomes captures uncertainty in short-range convective details and steering patterns over the next 48 hours.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Stable high-pressure systems and southerly advection of warm air masses are positioning Munich for peak temperatures near 34–36 °C on August 15.** Ensemble guidance from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) and German Weather Service (DWD) models shows minimal cloud cover and light winds under an omega-block pattern, enabling strong daytime solar insolation and surface heating. Recent observations confirm a regional heatwave with daytime maxima of 30–33 °C in southern Bavaria through mid-August, consistent with climatological late-summer warmth but elevated by the persistent ridge.

Market-implied odds heavily favor 35 °C (64.5 %) because short-range model runs converge on afternoon highs of 34–35 °C at official Munich stations, with lower probabilities for 34 °C or 36 °C reflecting typical forecast uncertainty ranges of ±1–2 °C. The German Weather Service’s final 24-hour maximum reading on August 15 will resolve the market, and any last-minute shifts in cloud cover or wind could adjust outcomes within the narrow 34–36 °C band. Traders are weighting the most recent model consensus and historical analogs for similar synoptic setups.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for Tokyo's highest temperature on August 16 centers on the 29–30°C range, reflecting a tight balance between seasonal heat and moderating factors like cloud cover and showers.** 

Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts for that Sunday show a maximum near 31°C under cloudy skies with occasional scattered showers, yet model variability in timing and extent of cloudiness keeps probabilities split between 29°C and 30°C. A strengthened Pacific High is sustaining above-normal summer temperatures across Honshu, but localized reductions in solar insolation from increased moisture and potential convective activity can trim peak readings by 1–2°C. Tokyo’s urban heat island effect amplifies baseline warmth, while high humidity (often exceeding 75%) influences perceived conditions without altering the official dry-bulb maximum. With resolution hinging on precise observational data from the Japan Meteorological Agency, the narrow spread between leading outcomes captures uncertainty in short-range convective details and steering patterns over the next 48 hours.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Stable high-pressure systems and southerly advection of warm air masses are positioning Munich for peak temperatures near 34–36 °C on August 15.** Ensemble guidance from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) and German Weather Service (DWD) models shows minimal cloud cover and light winds under an omega-block pattern, enabling strong daytime solar insolation and surface heating. Recent observations confirm a regional heatwave with daytime maxima of 30–33 °C in southern Bavaria through mid-August, consistent with climatological late-summer warmth but elevated by the persistent ridge.

Market-implied odds heavily favor 35 °C (64.5 %) because short-range model runs converge on afternoon highs of 34–35 °C at official Munich stations, with lower probabilities for 34 °C or 36 °C reflecting typical forecast uncertainty ranges of ±1–2 °C. The German Weather Service’s final 24-hour maximum reading on August 15 will resolve the market, and any last-minute shifts in cloud cover or wind could adjust outcomes within the narrow 34–36 °C band. Traders are weighting the most recent model consensus and historical analogs for similar synoptic setups.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office and ECMWF guidance indicate the mid-August heatwave peaking near 33–35 °C on 13–14 August will ease by the weekend, with high pressure relaxing and a shift toward more typical south-westerly flow. Key variables include exact timing of any frontal passage, boundary-layer moisture, and local station readings under variable insolation; forecasters note modest spread across ensembles, keeping lower (≤24 °C) and higher (≥28 °C) outcomes viable but less favored. Traders weigh these meteorological thresholds against climatological August averages near 21–23 °C, with fresh model runs expected before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Market-implied odds favor a narrow range around 29–30°C for Tokyo’s August 16 maximum, reflecting tight clustering in short-range numerical weather models.** The Japan Meteorological Agency and global ensembles currently project daytime highs near or slightly above the long-term August normal of ~31°C, driven by persistent influence of the strengthened Pacific High that has delivered above-normal temperatures across Honshu this summer. Subtle differences between 29°C and 30°C hinge on forecast details such as the exact timing and coverage of any scattered afternoon showers, boundary-layer mixing depth, and local urban heat-island effects that can add 1–2°C in central Tokyo districts. With resolution only two days away, traders are weighting the latest JMA and ECMWF runs most heavily; any shift in the 12–36-hour guidance on cloud cover or wind could quickly tip the balance between the two leading outcomes.
